intro: Long ago, a race was simple. Runners dashed down a straight dirt path at Olympia, and judges named who came first. Swimmers raced in the sea and in rivers. Rich players hit balls in walled palace courts. None of these could be measured the same way twice.

In this unit, you will see how three sports got their measured rooms. Track got a 400-meter lap, staggered lanes and clocks. Swimming got built pools, lane lines and separate records for each pool length. Tennis moved from an indoor palace game to a painted rectangle on grass.

You will also read the Illinois record books. They show when each state title began, and who was left out for many years. By the end, you will be able to explain how a shared length and a shared clock let two towns compare their athletes fairly.
bigQuestion: How did clocks, ropes and painted lines let people in different places compare races and games fairly?

test.q: What was the first race at Olympia?
test.why: By tradition, the first games had one footrace, one stade long.

test.q: Which Greek writer recorded Coroebus as the first winner?
test.why: Pausanias recorded that tradition in the 100s CE.

test.q: Why did tracks switch from 440 yards to 400 meters?
choices: So times could sit on one shared list.
test.why: One shared lap length lets times be compared.

test.q: Where was the IAAF, now World Athletics, formed in 1912?
test.why: The IAAF formed in Stockholm in 1912.

choices: makes every lane the same distance around a curve
test.why: Staggered marks even out the longer outer lanes.

test.q: Which Olympics first raced on a synthetic track?
test.why: Mexico City in 1968 used the first Olympic synthetic track.

test.q: What replaced hand stopwatches for world records in short races from 1977?
test.why: From 1977, the IAAF required fully automatic timing for those records.

test.q: From what year do IHSA records list state track champions?
test.why: IHSA records list track champions from 1893, before the IHSA was founded in 1900.

test.q: Where did Olympic swimmers first race in a built pool?
test.why: London built a 100-meter pool inside its stadium in 1908.

test.q: What does a touchpad on a pool wall do?
test.why: A touchpad stops the clock when a swimmer touches it.

test.q: Which is correct about Wingfield's lawn tennis?
test.why: Wingfield introduced his game in 1873 and patented it in 1874.

test.q: Who won the first Wimbledon, in 1877?
test.why: Spencer Gore won the first Wimbledon.
Girls swimming and diving began in 1975.

test.q: Which IHSA series began the same year as Title IX?
test.why: IHSA girls tennis and Title IX both date to 1972.

write.prompt: Pick one sport from this unit: track, swimming or tennis. How did a shared measurement make it possible to compare athletes in different places? Name two dates and two records, such as Pausanias's Description of Greece, the World Athletics rule book, Wingfield's 1874 patent, the 1877 Wimbledon rules or the IHSA record books. Then explain who was left out, and when that changed.
tips: Name each date and the document or record it comes from.
Say what things were like before the shared measurement, then after.
Use unit words such as stagger, long course or patent.
Include the people who were shut out and the year the door opened.
